gaps.sentence: It is Saturday tomorrow, so I ___ get up early.
gaps.hint: an absence of obligation at weekends
gaps.explanation: 'Don't have to' shows there is no obligation: don't have to get up.

gaps.sentence: Visitors ___ leave any bags unattended; security removes them at once.
gaps.explanation: 'Must not' expresses prohibition; 'need not' would mean it is optional.

gaps.sentence: ___ we need to book, or can we just turn up?
gaps.explanation: 'Need to' is a normal verb, so questions take 'do': Do we need.

gaps.sentence: You ___ seen the consultant's report — it is confidential and you have no clearance.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have + participle' expresses certainty that something did not happen.

gaps.sentence: He ___ be hungry — he has just eaten a three-course meal.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' rules out the possibility based on evidence: can't be hungry.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ to buy the textbook; copies are available in the library.
gaps.explanation: 'Don't have to' plus the infinitive expresses absence of obligation: don't have to buy.

gaps.sentence: You ___ touch that wire — it carries a live current!
gaps.explanation: 'Mustn't' signals something absolutely not allowed: mustn't touch.

gaps.sentence: He ___ have driven so fast on that icy road — he is lucky to be unhurt.
gaps.explanation: 'Shouldn't have' criticizes dangerous past behavior: shouldn't have.
